waypoints.title: Sgr B2 Deep South
waypoints.description: JWST NIRCam, background-subtracted: f480m-f410m in red, f405n-f410m in green, f187n-f182m in blue. The three fields below are the regions Nazar Budaiev picked out in Sgr B2 Deep South.

waypoints.title: Field 1 - JWST
waypoints.description: 5.5 arcsec across. Red is the 4.8 micron excess, tracing warm dust and shocked gas along the filament; the white contours are the ALMA moment-0 map at 0.05, 0.15, 0.30, 0.525 and 0.8625.

waypoints.title: Field 1 - ALMA
waypoints.description: The same 5.5 arcsec of sky in ALMA 1.3 mm continuum at 0.15 arcsec resolution. Two compact sources sit on the filament that the infrared only hints at.

waypoints.title: Field 2 - JWST
waypoints.description: 6.4 arcsec across. A bright star with strong diffraction spikes sits right next to the millimeter peak.

waypoints.title: Field 2 - ALMA
waypoints.description: In the millimeter the bright infrared star vanishes and a single compact source lights up at the contour peak: a protostar still inside its envelope.

waypoints.title: Field 3 - JWST
waypoints.description: 9 arcsec across, further south. Fainter and more extended, with a ridge running north-south through the field.

waypoints.title: Field 3 - ALMA
waypoints.description: A chain of compact millimeter sources runs along that ridge - a line of protostars in a filament that is nearly invisible in the infrared.

waypoints.title: Back Out
waypoints.description: Three fields, 5 to 9 arcsec each, out of a cloud spanning arcminutes. Star formation in Deep South is distributed along filaments rather than concentrated in the classic cores.
